# Twent Docs

> Step-by-step guides for Twent AI agent on Android — automate apps, run Ubuntu terminal & connect 1000+ services.

# Introduction
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs

Twent runs on **Android 8.0+** and gives you a real AI assistant that can see your screen, control any app, run shell commands, browse the web, manage files, and connect to external tools — all from one app. The agent can also install MCP servers and skills for itself, delegate to subagents, and ask you for clarification before hard decisions.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Start Using Twent" href="/getting-started/start-using-twent" icon="download">
    Download the APK, install Twent, grant permissions, and connect an AI provider — step by step.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Plugins" href="/plugins/mcp" icon="puzzle">
    Extend the agent with MCP servers and Skills.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Features" href="/features/agent-capabilities" icon="zap">
    Web research, persistent memory, Agent CLIs, Token Config, and the built-in Ubuntu terminal.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Glossary" href="/more/glossary" icon="book-open">
    Plain-English explanations of every technical term used in these docs.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Why Twent exists

Most AI assistants live in a chat bubble and can't touch your device. Twent is different — it runs **on your phone** with full access to the OS, giving AI real agency: reading your screen, tapping buttons, running commands, and managing files.

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Local-First" icon="shield">
    All data stays on your device. BYOK model — your keys, your data.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Free to Use" icon="gift">
    Twent is completely free. Paid model API usage is billed by your chosen provider. If someone asks you to pay for Twent itself, it's a scam.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Extensible" icon="plug">
    MCP servers, plugins, skills, and workflows for infinite capability.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Persistent Memory" icon="brain">
    The agent remembers relevant details across conversations, and its memory grows over time.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Customizable" icon="palette">
    Customize both the app UI and the AI agent's behavior to match your workflow.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Privacy First" icon="lock">
    Zero hidden telemetry. Nothing leaves your device except your explicit API calls.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Quick start

1. **Download & install the APK**

    Follow [Start Using Twent](/getting-started/start-using-twent) — download link, "install unknown apps", and Play Protect workarounds included.

2. **Grant permissions & pick a provider**

    Allow everything on the Permissions page, then add an API key under Settings → Model Settings (Nous Research, Opencode Zen, or NVIDIA NIMS are good starts).

3. **Wait for terminal setup**

    Open the Terminal page once — setup takes 8–10 minutes and runs by itself.

4. **Start searching**

    Start the ddg-search server under Plugins → MCP, then ask Twent anything.

# Agent Capabilities
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/features/agent-capabilities

## 1 · Search and research the web

Through the built-in **ddg-search** [MCP server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro), your Twent agent can search the web and research topics on your behalf.

:::note
Start the ddg-search server first if it isn't running — see the [Start Using Twent](/getting-started/start-using-twent) page.
:::

## 2 · Persistent memory

Twent has its own memory. It remembers things across chat sessions, and its memory grows over time the more you use it.

You stay in control — view, edit, or clear everything the AI remembers in the **"AI's Memory"** page in the app.

---

# Agent CLIs
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/features/agent-clis

An [Agent CLI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command-line_interface) is an AI agent that runs as a program in a terminal instead of in a chat app — tools like Claude Code or Codex that read, write, and run code for you.

The **Agent CLIs** page of Twent lets you browse all the supported agent CLIs and install them with one tap into the built-in [Ubuntu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubuntu) terminal:

- claude-code
- codex
- hermes-agent
- amp-code
- pi-agent
- roo-code
- kilocode
- …and more

:::tip
Make sure your [Terminal setup](/features/terminal) has completed first.
:::

---

# Bots
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/features/bots

Bots are essentially [AI agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligent_agent) that are given a specific task — and they keep doing it without you having to ask each time. You can create a bot yourself, or your Twent agent can create one on your behalf.

## Triggers

Each bot runs on one of three trigger types:

- **Manual** — you press run whenever you want it
- **Schedule-based** — runs automatically on a schedule you set
- **Event-based** — runs when something happens (an event fires)

## Managing bots

All of your bots appear in the app alongside the agent's work — see the **"Bots & Tasks"** page for the bird's-eye overview (covered in [Subagents](/features/subagents)).

:::tip
A bot is just an agent plus a task plus a trigger — describe what should happen and when, and let Twent handle the rest.
:::

---

# Subagents
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/features/subagents

The Twent agent can delegate **subagents** — helper agents that carry out the specific tasks the main agent assigns them. This lets bigger jobs get split into pieces and done while the main agent stays focused on coordinating.

## Where to see them

Bots and subagents can both be viewed from the **"Bots & Tasks"** page, which gives you a bird's-eye view of everything through a calendar-like UI.

## Related

- [Bots](/features/bots) — scheduled and event-triggered agents you set up yourself

---

# Terminal
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/features/terminal

The **Terminal** page is where an entire [Ubuntu Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubuntu) environment lives, right inside the Twent app. Both you and your agent can use it to install software, run scripts, manage files, and more.

## First-time setup

The moment you open the Terminal page for the very first time after installing Twent, setup starts **automatically**. It takes about **8–10 minutes**, so leave the app open and let it finish.

:::note[What gets installed?]
Once setup is complete, tap the **"Environment Setup"** button in the bottom-right corner of the Terminal page to see exactly what was installed during those 8–10 minutes.
:::

Many other features depend on this setup being done — including starting MCP servers ([Plugins → MCP](/plugins/mcp)) and installing [Agent CLIs](/features/agent-clis).

---

# Token Config
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/features/token-config

An [API key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API_key) ("token") is what connects Twent to an [AI model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model) provider.

The **Token Config** page lets you get the key for any provider of your choice **from that provider's own website, right inside the Twent app** — no juggling between your phone browser, email, and the app. Sign up or log in on the provider's page, generate the key, and Twent picks it up.

Prefer to configure manually? You can always paste keys yourself under **Settings → Model Settings** (see [Start Using Twent](/getting-started/start-using-twent)).

---

# Start Using Twent
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/getting-started/start-using-twent

Everything you need to go from download to your first working AI agent on your phone. If any word below feels unfamiliar (APK, API key, MCP…), click it — every technical term is linked to a plain-English explanation, and they are all collected on the [Glossary](/more/glossary) page.

## Step 1 · Download the APK

An [APK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apk) is the installation file for Android apps — like a `.exe` installer on Windows.

[Download twent.apk (~80 MB)](https://assets.twent.xyz/twent.apk)

Or copy this address into your phone's browser: **https://assets.twent.xyz/twent.apk**

## Step 2 · Allow "Install unknown apps"

Because Twent isn't from the [Google Play Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Play), Android blocks installs by default. This is normal — installing apps outside the store is called [sideloading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sideloading).

1. Tap the downloaded `twent.apk` file.
2. Your phone will say the install is blocked and offer **Settings**.
3. In that settings screen, turn ON **"Allow from this source"** for your browser (this is the *install unknown apps* permission — official Google explanation [here](https://support.google.com/android/answer/9437081)).
4. Go back and tap `twent.apk` again to install.

## Step 3 · Install Twent

Tap `twent.apk` once more and press **Install**.

:::note[If you see a "Play Protect" warning]
[Play Protect](https://support.google.com/googleplay/answer/2812853) is Google's scanner — it often flags apps that aren't from the Play Store, even safe ones. To continue:

1. Open the **Play Store**
2. Tap your **profile picture** (top right)
3. Tap **Play Protect**
4. Tap **Pause Play Protect** and enter your phone password
5. Tap the `twent.apk` file again to install
:::

<video src="https://res.cloudinary.com/dcpcpoyzj/video/upload/v1787466575/lv_0_20260823112114_se0sch.mp4" controls muted playsinline style="width:100%;border-radius:12px;" />

*The same install-and-setup walkthrough video shown on [twent.xyz/apk](https://twent.xyz/apk).*

## Step 4 · Grant permissions

When Twent opens for the first time you land on the **Permissions** page. Allow **all** of them — they power screen reading, automation, files, and the terminal. You can optionally sign in with Google, but there's no added benefit yet.

## Step 5 · Connect an AI provider

Twent is BYOK — bring your own key. An [API key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API_key) is a password-like string that lets Twent talk to an [AI model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model) provider, which does the actual thinking.

1. Go to **Settings** → tap the **Model Settings** card
2. Pick a **Provider**, paste an **API key**, and choose a **Model**

Good options:

| Provider | Get a key from | Why pick it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nous Research | [portal.nousresearch.com](https://portal.nousresearch.com) | Fast responses, very generous free tier, constant free promos |
| Opencode Zen | [opencode.ai/zen](https://opencode.ai/zen) | Faster responses, generous free tier |
| NVIDIA NIMS | [build.nvidia.com/models](https://build.nvidia.com/models) | Access to many [open-weights models](https://huggingface.co/models); slower responses |

## Step 6 · Wait for terminal setup

Open the **Terminal** page. A full [Ubuntu Linux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubuntu) environment sets itself up automatically the first time — this takes **8–10 minutes**, so let it run. Details on the [Terminal](/features/terminal) page.

## Step 7 · Start the web-search server

Once the terminal setup is finished, go to **Plugins → MCP tab**, find the built-in **ddg-search** server, and start it. This gives the agent web search. More on the [MCP](/plugins/mcp) page.

## Done 🎉

You're set. Try asking Twent something, or explore what it can do on [Agent Capabilities](/features/agent-capabilities).

---

# Data Deletion Instructions
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/legal/data-deletion

App Name: **Twent**


## How to Delete Your Data


 Twent is a local-first application. We do not store your personal data,
 chat history, or agentic memory on our own servers. All your data is
 stored locally on your device. To delete your data, please follow these
 steps:


## Option 1 (In-App)


 Open the Twent app, navigate to Settings, and tap the "Clear All Local
 Data" button.


## Option 2 (Android System)


 Go to your Android device Settings > Apps > Twent > Storage
 & cache > tap Clear Storage (or Clear Data).


## What Data is Deleted


 Executing the steps above will permanently and immediately delete all
 locally stored data, including:

Chat history and conversation logs.
 Agentic memory and knowledge base entries.
 Saved workflows, templates, and local configurations.
## What Data is Kept / Third-Party Data


 Because Twent operates on a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) model, your
 prompts and files are sent directly to the third-party AI providers you
 choose (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic). Twent does not retain this data. Any
 data processed by these third-party providers is subject to their
 respective privacy policies and data retention practices.

---

# Glossary
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/more/glossary

The Twent docs use some technical words. Here's what each one means — the same terms are clickable wherever they appear in these docs.

| Term | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| [APK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apk) | The installation file for Android apps — like an installer on a PC. |
| [Sideloading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sideloading) | Installing an app from outside the official Play Store. |
| [Play Protect](https://support.google.com/googleplay/answer/2812853) | Google's app scanner. It sometimes warns about apps that aren't from the Play Store, even safe ones. |
| [Permission](https://support.google.com/android/answer/9431959) | A capability you grant an app — camera, storage, seeing your screen, etc. |
| [API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API) | "Application Programming Interface" — a way for two programs to talk to each other. |
| [API key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API_key) | A secret password-like string that identifies you to an online service. Twent uses one to talk to your AI provider. |
| [AI model / LLM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model) | The "brain" that powers AI chat — e.g. GPT, Claude, or open models like Llama. |
| [Provider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_chatbots#Large_language_models) | A company that serves AI models through its API (e.g. Nous Research, NVIDIA). |
| [Open-weights model](https://huggingface.co/models) | An AI model anyone can download and run themselves. |
| BYOK | "Bring Your Own Key" — the app is free; you supply your own provider API key. |
| [Ubuntu / Linux terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubuntu) | A text interface to a full Linux operating system — here, running inside Twent on your phone. |
| [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro) | Model Context Protocol — an open standard for giving AI agents extra tools (search, GitHub, databases…). |
| [MCP server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/architecture) | One tool package speaking MCP. Can be hosted online or run locally on your phone. |
| STDIO | An MCP server that runs as a local program on your device rather than on the internet. |
| streamable-http | An MCP server hosted on the internet that Twent talks to over the network. |
| [Skill](https://agentskills.io) | A ready-made instruction pack that teaches the agent how to do a specific job well. |
| [CLI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command-line_interface) | Command-Line Interface — a program you drive by typing commands instead of tapping buttons. |
| Agent CLI | An AI agent (like Claude Code) that runs as a CLI program in a terminal. |

---

# Memory
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/more/memory

Persistent knowledge storage that survives across conversations. The AI
remembers your preferences, past discussions, and important information, and its memory grows over time.

## Memory Types

 **User Preferences** — communication style, apps,
contacts

 **Conversation Summaries** — key decisions and action
items

 **Knowledge Base** — notes, reference material, research

## Memory Tools


| Tool | Description |
| --- | --- |
| memory_search | Search across all memories |
| memory_save | Save new information |
| memory_update | Update existing memories |
| memory_link | Create relationships between memories |

 All memories are stored **locally** on your device. Nothing
leaves your device except API calls.

| Interface | Theme, display, language, layout |
| Intelligence | API usage, context, summarization |

## Model Configuration


 Support for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, OpenRouter, LM Studio, and local
 MNN/llama.cpp models. Configure temperature, max tokens, and other
 parameters per model.


## Themes


 Full visual customization — colors, fonts, spacing, wallpapers. Create
 custom themes and share them. Configure at `Settings → Theme`
 .

# Tool Reference
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/more/tool-reference

Complete parameter reference for all built-in tools.

## read_file


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| path | string | Yes | File path |
| offset | number | No | Start line (1-indexed) |
| limit | number | No | Max lines (default: 500) |


## write_file


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| path | string | Yes | File path |
| content | string | Yes | Content to write |


## terminal


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| command | string | Yes | Command to run |
| timeout | number | No | Max seconds |
| workdir | string | No | Working directory |
| background | boolean | No | Run in background |
| pty | boolean | No | Interactive mode |


## tap


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ref | string | Yes | Element reference ID (@e5) |


## swipe


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| startX | number | Yes | Start X |
| startY | number | Yes | Start Y |
| endX | number | Yes | End X |
| endY | number | Yes | End Y |
| duration | number | No | Duration in ms |


## type


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | string | Yes | Text to type |
| ref | string | No | Element to type into |


## scroll


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direction | string | Yes | up, down, left, right |


## press_key


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| key | string | Yes | back, home, volume_up, etc. |


## open_app


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| packageName | string | Yes | Android package name |


## fetch_url


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| url | string | Yes | URL to fetch |
| max_length | number | No | Max characters |


## memory_search


| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| query | string | Yes | Search query |
| limit | number | No | Max results |

| --- | --- |

 Set a custom trigger phrase in
 `Settings → Speech Services → Wake Word`. The device listens
 for the phrase and starts recording your command.

# MCP
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/plugins/mcp

[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro) (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for plugging extra tools into an AI agent. An [MCP server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/architecture) can do anything from web search to GitHub management, and Twent speaks it natively.

## Server types Twent accepts

Twent works with two kinds of MCP servers:

- **streamable-http** — servers hosted somewhere on the internet; Twent talks to them over the network
- **STDIO** — servers that run as a small program right on your phone (inside the built-in terminal)

## Authentication: the three flavors

**1. Browser-based login** — some servers let you sign in through a browser flow, like a normal "Log in with…" button. [GitHub's MCP server](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server), for example.

**2. Auth token** — others need you to paste a credential ([an API key or access token](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API_key)) into that server's configuration. The Apify server works this way.

**3. No authentication** — some remotely-hosted servers need nothing at all, like `https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp`. And some run **entirely locally** on your phone, like the built-in **ddg-search** server.

## Discovering servers

You don't have to hunt for configs yourself:

- Browse and search **publicly-published MCP servers** from sources like [GitHub](https://github.com/topic/model-context-protocol) and [mcpservers.org](https://mcpservers.org) — right inside the MCP section of Twent
- Your Twent agent can also **install and run MCP servers on demand**, if it thinks one would help with the task at hand

## Managing servers

- Everything you've installed appears in the **"My Servers"** section of the MCP tab
- Servers can be enabled and disabled from the same tab

:::tip[Start here]
The built-in **ddg-search** server gives your agent web search. Start it once your [terminal setup](/features/terminal) has finished — see [Start Using Twent](/getting-started/start-using-twent).
:::

---

# Skills
Source: https://twent.xyz/docs/plugins/skills

Skills are ready-made instruction packs that teach your agent how to do specific jobs well — writing styles, workflows, tool recipes. Find them under **Plugins → Skills tab**.

## Browsing and installing

Browse through and search the skill catalog right inside the Skills tab. Once installed, your Twent agent can call those skills whenever they're useful.

## Tagging a skill with "/"

Want the agent to use a particular skill? Type `/` at the start of your prompt followed by the skill's name, and Twent will make the agent refer to exactly that skill.

Example: typing `/copywriting Write a launch tweet` points the agent straight at the copywriting skill.

## My section

Everything you've installed appears in the **"My"** section of the Skills tab.

:::note
Your Twent agent can also install and use skills **on demand** — when it thinks a skill would help with what you asked.
:::
